sovereign_country.strategic_role: 海湾阿拉伯国家自贸走廊、外资100%控股与印度洋海运枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Discretionary Portfolio Advisory for Multiple Private Client Families

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Sultanate of Oman (national, unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid civil-law legal system rooted in codified statute (Commercial Code and Commercial Companies Law) with Islamic Sharia as a residual source of law; unified national corporate registry without sub-federal variations
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US - Oman Free Trade Agreement (in force since 1 January 2009)
GCC Unified Economic Agreement (Oman as member state)
Bilateral investment promotion and protection treaties in force with the United Kingdom, Germany, France, the Netherlands, China, India, Japan and other jurisdictions
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements in force with more than 40 jurisdictions, including the United Kingdom, India, the Netherlands, and Singapore
US - Oman trade and investment framework arrangements ancillary to the FTA

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Companies Law, Royal Decree No. 18/2019 (Articles 111-120 governing the Single Person Company, together with corporate name and register provisions); Foreign Capital Investment Law, Royal Decree No. 50/2019 (permitting 100% foreign ownership); Law on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, Royal Decree No. 30/2016, as amended in 2020 and 2022 (UBO identification, PEP duties, record-keeping and reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit and the National Committee for AML/CFT); Executive Regulations of Royal Decree No. 30/2016; Capital Market Law, Royal Decree No. 80/1998, as amended, and the AML/CFT standards of the Capital Market Authority now administered by the Financial Services Authority of Oman (Royal Decree No. 38/2022 consolidation); Central Bank of Oman AML regulations applicable to transaction banks; UN Security Council resolutions implemented domestically; UBO registration obligation effected through the MoCIIP Commercial Registry and the Invest Easy portal.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of the founding foreign shareholder and all ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or competent attestation authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Apostille Convention (Oman a contracting party since 12 February 2023); alternatively consular legalization through the Omani embassy for non-contracting states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate constitutional documents of the ultimate parent entity (certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association) and board resolutions authorizing the Oman SPC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternative consular legalization and Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation in Muscat; certified Arabic translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / police clearance certificate for the founding shareholder, resident manager, and all UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal-records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by certified Arabic translation and Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and sworn source-of-funds / source-of-wealth affirmation supporting the initial capitalization of the multi-family office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating licensed bank or private-wealth institution and the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the origin country, apostille, and certified Arabic translation for the MoCIIP and FSA files

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Omani corporate services agent and resident manager for pre-incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary of the jurisdiction where the power of attorney is signed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified Arabic translation and attestation by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Muscat

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT beneficial-ownership declaration and PEP questionnaire covering shareholders, directors-in-fact, and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholder, authenticated before a public notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, apostille or consular legalization, and certification by a licensed Omani translator; retained in the company AML/CFT register

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Oman's domestic terrorism and sanctions list maintained by the Financial Intelligence Unit and the National Committee for AML/CFT, OFAC SDN and sectoral screening (required for USD SWIFT and custody rails), EU and UK consolidated lists, and GCC designated-persons listing. All UBOs, the founding shareholder, the resident manager and authorized signatories must complete enhanced PEP due diligence (domestic and foreign PEPs, family members and close associates), with independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, risk-based periodic refreshment, and audit-trail retention of screening evidence under Royal Decree No. 30/2016 and the FSA/CMA AML rules. A compliance sign-off is required before submission of the incorporation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Invest Easy (investeasy.gov.om) - official single-window commercial registry and licensing portal of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP); supplementary publication in the Official Gazette of the Sultanate of Oman
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be formulated and registered in Modern Standard Arabic; a Latin-script transliteration may be recorded as a secondary commercial style provided it is phonetically and graphically consistent with the Arabic name. All statutory filings, notarial deeds and the Articles of Association must be in Arabic, with foreign-language attachments accompanied by certified Arabic translations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words denoting the Sultan, members of the royal family, or 'Sultanate'
The word 'Oman' or state emblems implying official sponsorship
Names of foreign states, heads of state, or international governmental organizations
Bank (prior Central Bank of Oman approval required)
Insurance (prior Financial Services Authority approval required)
Investment, Portfolio, or Advisory (triggers FSA/CMA scrutiny for the multi-family office scope; a regulator-specific nomination is required)
Ministry, ministerial titles, or terms suggesting government affiliation
Religious references and terms contrary to public order and morality
Offensive, misleading, or commercially deceptive terms, including 'Family Office' without supporting regulatory license documentation
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered Commercial Registry name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may apply online through Invest Easy for one extension of the reservation before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative objection with the Commercial Registry Directorate within 15 working days, attaching evidence of consent, trademark rights, goodwill, or rectification of misleading elements. If the objection is denied, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the competent Administrative Court in Muscat within 60 days under Omani administrative procedure rules; interim name protection may be preserved only through a court order. The multi-family office applicant should simultaneously coordinate the FSA/CMA no-objection statement to remove any regulatory-token objection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. The Commercial Registry requires a substantive Oman address evidenced by a notarized lease or title document; an aggregator address is tolerated only for non-regulated holding functions. For the licensed multi-family office, a virtual office is impermissible: the FSA/CMA substance rules require a dedicated physical office in Oman, named compliance and investment officers, and operating premises identifiable for client due-diligence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. The FSA/CMA conducts pre-licensing substance surveys and unpredictable on-site inspections for licensed investment businesses (probability above 70% within the first 12 months of licensing); MoCIIP and the municipality further verify the registered office upon renewal and upon third-party complaints, producing approximately 100% inspection coverage at the license stage.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced due diligence PEP and sanctions screening run (UN, OFAC, EU, UK, GCC, Omani FIA lists) for all UBOs and authorized signatories

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per screened individual or entity

Registered physical office - initial quarter rent, notarized lease registration, municipality and landlord fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rental benchmark and statutory municipality tariffs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the Sultanate of Oman, promulgated by Royal Decree No. 18/2019 (as amended), Single Person Company (SPC) and Limited Liability Company provisions; Foreign Capital Investment Law, Royal Decree No. 50/2019 (permitting 100% foreign ownership); Capital Market Law, Royal Decree No. 80/1998 and Financial Services Authority (FSA) licensing directives governing the regulated financial activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) of the Sultanate of Oman — Commercial Registry, Muscat.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized SPC Memorandum of Association (MoA) together with the standard MoCIIP company registration application lodged through the Invest Easy single-window e-portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum subscribed or paid-up capital for an SPC under Royal Decree 18/2019; the sole member fixes the capital in the MoA. For the discretionary portfolio-management licence, the Financial Services Authority (FSA) imposes a minimum regulatory capital (typically not less than OMR 250,000 or such higher amount as FSA determines), which must be deposited with a Central Bank of Oman (CBO) regulated bank and evidenced by a certificate; pending licence issuance the capital remains held in a blocked escrow-style account releasable only with FSA consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Single Person Company (SPC) is validly organized under the Companies Law of Oman (Royal Decree 18/2019), and that its Memorandum of Association, executed before the notary public, is hereby adopted. RESOLVED, that the subscribed share capital be ratified, and that the registered office be established at Muscat, Sultanate of Oman. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Sole Manager and principal compliance officer, with full authority to open and operate bank accounts, designate signatories, and instruct professional advisers. RESOLVED, that the Sole Manager file for tax registration, Oman Chamber of Commerce membership, Financial Services Authority licensing, and all municipal, civil-defense, environmental and regulatory approvals, and execute all ancillary documents on behalf of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Activity Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Commercial Registry — Invest Easy single-window e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-reservation application in Arabic and English proposing three alternative trading names. State the SPC legal form and the restricted financial-services activity (discretionary portfolio advisory for multiple family offices) using the MoCIIP activity classification corresponding to ISIC 6430 / NAICS 523920. Pay the statutory name-reservation fee electronically upon submission. Obtain the name-approval slip and activity pre-approval before executing the MoA.
required_dossiers: Completed name-reservation application form
Copy of the sole member's passport (foreign national)
Notarized power of attorney authorizing the applicant representative
Corporate authorization resolution and certificate of good standing if the sole member is a corporate entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, refile with alternative names within 15 days. If rejection is based on policy or activity grounds, lodge a written administrative objection with the MoCIIP Commercial Registry Review Committee within 30 days, attaching the FSA in-principle approval to evidence that the activity is licensable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization and Attestation of the SPC Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public under the Ministry of Justice; MoCIIP attestation unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the bilingual Arabic/English MoA using the Ministry-standard SPC template, including the sole member's particulars, subscribed capital, office address, manager appointment, and permitted objects. Arrange execution by the sole member or attorney-in-fact before a licensed notary public; obtain notarial certification and stamping of every page. Submit the notarized MoA for MoCIIP attestation where required, and retain a certified Arabic original for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Name-approval slip and activity pre-approval letter
Draft MoA in Arabic and English
Notarized power of attorney of the sole member
Passport copies of the sole member and appointed manager
Proof of registered office address (preliminary letter of intent or lease preview)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags identity or authority deficiencies, legalize or apostille the underlying corporate resolutions and re-execute before the notary. Correction resubmission may be made within 10 days; a fresh attestation cycle is required for amended MoA pages.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Commercial Registry — Invest Easy corporate filing module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized and attested MoA, the name-approval slip, and identification documents of the sole member and manager. Declare the subscribed capital and confirm the SPC legal form with limited liability. Select the regulated activity code and, if prompted, attach the FSA in-principle approval or a declaration that licensed operation will not commence before the FSA licence is issued. Pay the CR issuance fee and download the electronic Commercial Registration certificate upon approval.
required_dossiers: Notarized and attested MoA
Name-approval slip
Passport copies of the sole member and manager
Manager acceptance and undertaking letter
Declaration of capital and source of funds
FSA in-principle approval (if obtained) or regulatory status declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to MoCIIP queries within 15 working days by uploading clarifications or corrected documents. If the application is rejected, request a written statement of reasons and file an administrative appeal with the Undersecretary for Commerce within 30 days, or re-file after curing the stated defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Oman Chamber of Commerce Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Tax Authority — E-Services Portal; Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued CR certificate, apply through the Tax Authority E-Services portal for the Tax Registration Number (TRN), submitting the MoA, CR, and office address. After TRN allocation, file the OCCI membership application with the CR number and activity description, remit the membership fee, and obtain the OCCI membership certificate used for municipal licensing and subsequent labour visa processing.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized MoA
Passport copies of the sole member and manager
Tax Authority registration form (translated and verified)
Attested office lease agreement or utility bill
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TRN application is suspended for incomplete data, correct and resubmit within 10 days. If OCCI membership is withheld due to activity-code mismatch, obtain an amended CR extract and re-file; OCCI refusal may be administratively reconsidered upon production of the updated CR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Regulatory Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the SPC bank account at a licensed Omani bank, presenting the CR, MoA, TRN, and OCCI certificate. Complete the customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership declaration. Deposit the subscribed share capital, and, where the FSA licence requires minimum regulatory capital, arrange for the required balance to be held in a blocked or escrow-style deposit subject to FSA release conditions. Obtain the bank capital deposit certificate and corporate banking mandate for signature control.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized MoA
Tax Registration Number confirmation
OCCI membership certificate
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declarations
Manager appointment resolution
Bank-prescribed KYC/KYB forms and board references
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence queries, supplement the submission with the group ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, and the FSA licence application receipt. If the account opening is declined, pursue the bank's internal appeal channel or select an alternative CBO-regulated bank and resubmit the corporate file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Authority of Oman — Securities and Investment Business Licensing Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the FSA licensing application for discretionary portfolio management and investment advisory services to multiple family offices. File the corporate constitutional documents, programme of operations, internal controls and AML/CFT manual, compliance and risk-management procedures, regulatory capital evidence, and fitness-and-propriety statements for senior management and the compliance officer. Attend FSA interview or site-visit if requested, and obtain the licence before commencing any regulated activity or holding client assets.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized MoA
Detailed business plan and operations manual
AML/CFT policy and internal control framework
Regulatory capital deposit certificate from the bank
Curriculum vitae, police clearances, and declarations of senior management
Compliance officer appointment and terms of reference
Conflicts-of-interest and outsourcing policies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to FSA information requests within 20 working days of notice. If the licence is refused, the company may re-apply after remediating the identified deficiencies, or invoke the FSA administrative review procedure within 30 days, supported by updated governance and capital documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Trade Licence, Civil Defence Clearance and Physical Premises Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Muscat Municipality or relevant governorate authority; Public Authority for Civil Defence and Ambulance (PACDA); Environment Authority (EA) single window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal trade licence application using the CR, OCCI certificate, and attested lease agreement. Submit the office floor plan for building-occupancy approval and arrange PACDA fire-safety inspection to obtain the fire-safety certificate. Register the activity with the Environment Authority under the Category 3 self-classification for office-based financial services, receiving the environmental registration confirmation. Obtain final municipal occupation and signage permits before physical operation.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate and OCCI membership certificate
Attested lease agreement
Municipal trade licence application form
Office floor plans and building occupancy certificate
PACDA fire-safety plan and inspection form
Environment Authority Category 3 self-assessment registration form
Façade signage permit application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PACDA flags fire-safety deficiencies, implement corrective measures (alarms, extinguishers, egress signage) and request re-inspection. If the municipality queries the lease or floor plan, submit corrected documents within 10 working days; adverse municipal decisions may be appealed to the municipal licensing committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Authority of Oman (FSA) — successor to the Capital Market Authority (CMA) for securities and investment-business licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Securities Business Licence — Discretionary Portfolio Management and Investment Advisory (Multi-Family Office) issued under the Capital Market Law (Royal Decree No. 80/1998) and applicable FSA licensing directives

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Authority (EA) of the Sultanate of Oman
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — No Significant Environmental Impact; automatic environmental registration for office-based financial services; no Full EIA Report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to industrial point-source discharges or VOC-emitting processes; office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer-disposal by-laws for domestic effluent, solid waste must be segregated and collected through municipal waste services, and any emergency standby generator must conform to Oman's ambient air-quality and noise limits applicable to commercial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: PACDA fire-safety certificate prior to occupation; municipal building-occupancy and structural-load approval by the competent municipality; Ministry of Labour occupational health and safety workplace clearance; emergency-evacuation plan, first-aid provisions, and annual renewal of the PACDA and municipal licences.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA), established as the independent national tax administration by Royal Decree 12/2023, succeeding the Secretariat General of Taxation within the Ministry of Finance; exclusively competent for corporate income tax (Royal Decree 28/2009 as amended), Value Added Tax (Royal Decree 121/2020 effective 16 April 2021), selective/excise tax, withholding tax compliance, and taxpayer registration. Unified electronic portal: 'Emtaaz' at https://emtaaz.ota.gov.om, interoperable with the Invest Easy company registration portal, the MOCIIP commercial register, and the Bayan customs clearance platform; the OTA issues the TIN, the annual tax card, VAT certificate, and export clearance attestations. No sub-national or municipal tax authority exists; the Sultanate is a Unitary_National jurisdiction for indirect tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Precondition: a foreign-owned Single Person Company (SPC) engaged as a Multi-Family Office (MFO) must first obtain the specialized statutory license from the Financial Services Authority (FSA) under Royal Decree 30/2023, or the Central Bank of Oman where deposit-taking or custodial activities are combined, because the tax file will not be approved without the underlying CR and FSA license. Step 1: incorporate the SPC with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) through Invest Easy; reserve the name and file the single-member LLC constitutional documents under the Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree 18/2019); obtain the Commercial Registration (CR) certificate. Step 2: within 30 days of CR issuance, apply through Emtaaz for income tax registration / the tax card; upload the CR, audited incorporation documents, the 100% foreign shareholder's passport and utility-lease evidence of the Oman office, the FSA license, the AML/CFT compliance framework, and bank reference from the Omani custodian bank; OTA then issues the Omani TIN and annual tax card. Step 3: VAT registration through the same Emtaaz profile is mandatory within 30 days after taxable supplies exceed OMR 38,500 in the current or immediately preceding 12-month period, or within 30 days after the SPC expects to exceed that threshold; the OTA issues the VAT certificate with the VAT identification number. Step 4: supplementary registrations include PASI social insurance, the Municipality fee account, and Oman Chamber of Commerce membership; the tax identification is automatically suspended if the FSA license or CR lapses, so the SPC must keep the professional license current at all times.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Omani SPC is a separate juridical and tax person, wholly distinct from its non-resident foreign shareholder; it is taxed as a resident Omani company under Article 2 of the Income Tax Law (RD 28/2009 as amended), with the headline corporate income tax rate of 15% applied to its worldwide/territorial profits arising from services managed, performed, and delivered in Oman. No pass-through treatment is available; the MFO cannot be treated as a transparent partnership or disregarded entity; there is no consolidated/group filing regime, so each SPC files separately. Territorial_Scope note: a resident SPC may exclude demonstrably non-Omani portfolio income only where management and control are exercised outside Oman and revenues are not attributable to Omani activity, but discretionary portfolio advisory physically performed by Oman-based investment staff remains Oman-sourced. Tax_Exempt_Zone: the mainland SPC is not automatically within the OPAZ free-zone regime; an MFO would not ordinarily qualify for free-zone income tax holidays (10-30 years) because financial services are not a qualifying core free-zone activity unless specific OPAZ approval and physical free-zone substance are first obtained, with all VAT and CIT consequences confirmed by binding OTA rulings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Oman does not operate a US-style check-the-box or tax classification election; entity tax status follows the legal form. Available statutory elections and administrative mechanisms: (i) VAT group registration under Article 9 of the VAT Law (RD 121/2020) and Article 14 of the VAT Executive Regulations, allowing the SPC and related Omani-resident entities with 50% or greater common control to be treated as a single VAT taxable person so that intra-group supplies are disregarded; (ii) voluntary VAT registration at the OMR 19,250 annual threshold; (iii) VAT special scheme for imported services under reverse-charge mechanisms (no Omani registration needed for the non-resident supplier); (iv) income tax depreciation method election between straight-line and declining-balance methods, applied consistently for fixed assets; (v) automatic five-year tax loss carry-forward under Article 35 of the Income Tax Law, with no formal election and no carry-back; (vi) accounting period election to a non-calendar fiscal year, subject to OTA approval; (vii) free-zone incentive application filed through OPAZ where the MFO can prove qualifying industrial/logistics activity; (viii) treaty relief / double-taxation-avoidance election for the foreign shareholder is a separate claim under Oman's tax treaty network (currently limited treaties; Oman's domestic law also grants relief for foreign tax paid on doubly taxed income where a DTT exists); no hybrid mismatch elections are available or required under Omani law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Law of the Value Added Tax, Royal Decree No. 121/2020, implemented by the VAT Executive Regulations, aligned with the GCC Unified VAT Agreement; Oman applies no separate sales-and-use tax, no municipal GST, and no services tax; VAT is the exclusive indirect tax in the mainland, while certain supplies made within licensed free zones are outside the scope of Omani VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration threshold: OMR 38,500 of annual taxable supplies in the last 12 months or reasonably expected in the next 12 months; voluntary registration threshold: OMR 19,250; non-resident suppliers have no threshold where the reverse charge applies, although the Omani recipient is liable to account for the VAT. An MFO advising multiple private family entities must aggregate the taxable value of all its supplies on a single taxable-person basis whenever connected family SPVs are supplied, and should consider VAT grouping to avoid break-up of the threshold; supply of exempt financial services is excluded from the taxable turnover computation but counts for monitoring the threshold where taxable supplies are mixed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The OTA is operating a phased national electronic invoicing (fiscal invoicing) mandate for VAT-registered persons, commencing with large taxpayers and progressively extending to all taxpayers including professional service companies such as an MFO. Compliant e-invoices must be issued and transmitted in real time through the OTA's approved e-invoice API/clearance environment in the prescribed structured data format (including TIN, buyer TIN or foreign tax ID, VAT amount, and supply classification); the system requires an OTA digital signature, a machine-readable QR code, and validation of the fiscal invoice before issuance to the client; post-clearance stamping returns a unique fiscal invoice identifier that must be included on the customer copy. The MFO must integrate its billing/ERP system with the OTA's clearance APIs and cannot rely on offline or paper invoicing for business-to-business supplies after its implementation wave; invoices to private family clients and to the Omani custodian bank are business-to-business fiscal invoices requiring full compliance; failure to clear e-invoices before issuance triggers rejection of the input VAT credit by the client and administrative penalties for the issuer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating is available where the goods are physically exported from Oman under the Bayan customs declaration within 90 days of supply, with title passing to a non-resident buyer. Services: for the MFO, the international B2B place-of-supply rule places discretionary portfolio management, asset allocation advisory, family-governance consulting, and reporting services supplied to a non-resident recipient outside Oman where the recipient is established outside Oman and is not present in Oman at the time of supply; such services are either zero-rated or treated as outside the scope of Omani VAT, preserving the MFO's recovery of input VAT on professional, licensing, and technology costs. To claim the 0% rate, the MFO must demonstrate that: (i) the client is non-resident (tax residency certificate or equivalent KYC documentation); (ii) benefit and performance are enjoyed outside Oman; (iii) services are not connected with Omani immovable property or an Omani fixed establishment of the client; and (iv) the fee consideration is received from abroad. Zero-rating is denied where the service contract is with an Omani-resident family trust, an Omani citizen resident in Oman, or a local SPV whose ultimate beneficiaries are Oman-domiciled, even if the family office is operated through offshore holding structures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bayan customs export declaration (electronic export declaration number and acceptance receipt), required only for physical goods but maintained as part of the complete VAT export file for any mixed service/product engagement
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from Omani territory within the 90-day export window
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation / custodian wire advice evidencing receipt of the export or service fee from outside Oman within the 180-day repatriation benchmark

Executed investment management agreement or service agreement identifying the non-resident client family, the offshore situs of the assets under management, and the fee basis for the zero-rated or outside-scope supply
E-invoice (OTA-cleared fiscal invoice) showing the zero-rated supply classification and the client's foreign tax identification number or certificate of tax residence
Client KYC/AML file with beneficial ownership documentation, the MFO's FSA license, and the custody mandate / power of attorney proving control over non-Omani custodian accounts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The OTA actively audits export zero-rating claims by MFOs and financial service providers. Where the exporter cannot produce the complete documentation bundle, fails to demonstrate the non-resident status of the recipient, or does not receive the consideration within the referenced 180-day window, the OTA will reverse the 0% treatment, charge 5% VAT on the gross fee, disallow any associated input VAT credits, and issue an additional-assessment with a monthly late-payment charge running from the original due date of the VAT return; administrative fines of up to OMR 10,000 per contravention may be imposed under the VAT Executive Regulations. In cases of deliberate misrepresentation, forged export documents, or circular offshore payment arrangements, the VAT Law (RD 121/2020) provides for criminal penalties of imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fines up to OMR 50,000, in addition to full recovery of the evaded tax and related interest; statute of limitations is five years in ordinary cases and longer where fraud is alleged. The OTA coordinates with the Central Bank of Oman and the FSA under AML/CFT channels, so cross-border fee repatriation for a High_Risk_Special_License MFO is examined for both tax authenticity and sanctions/beneficial-ownership integrity; any restructuring of fees by the foreign shareholder or related offshore entity is also subject to Omani transfer pricing adjustments and secondary disallowance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO) in conjunction with the Financial Services Authority (FSA) for securities-related fintech activities; the National Centre for Financial Information and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) oversee AML/CFT reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Omani Rial (OMR) is pegged to the USD at 1 OMR = 2.6008 USD. Oman accepts Article VIII obligations of the IMF, guaranteeing free convertibility for current international transactions. Capital account transactions are largely liberal but certain regime-bound items (bank borrowing, securities issuance) require CBO or FSA approval. Profit remittance and capital repatriation are permitted without exchange controls, subject to documentary compliance (tax clearance, audited financials, and purpose codes). No general restriction exists for non-resident ownership of Omani Single Person Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists under Omani law. Exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic licensed accounts indefinitely. Nevertheless, all export receipts must be routed through a licensed bank in the Sultanate; CBO AML/CFT directives require proper trade documentation (e.g., Bill of Lading, Invoice, Export Declaration) and repatriation within the commercial credit cycle. No fixed 30/60/90-day disposal timeline is imposed; however, banks apply a de facto 180-day expectation for routine trade transactions unless exceptional circumstances are justified.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not authorized by the Central Bank of Oman and cannot provide custodial or escrow services for regulated Omani entities. They may be used as supplementary outbound payment instruments for non-settlement transactions, but they are not acceptable for statutory capital deposits, tax disbursements, or high-value family office transfers. Practical limitations include absence of OMR clearing, lack of CBO oversight, and high probability of correspondent de-risking. A licensed Omani commercial bank account remains the sole viable treasury spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for all authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of a Multi-Family Office. Omani banks require an in-person KYC interview at the branch, or at an Oman-based embassy/consulate with a notarized power-of-attorney, plus a direct video call with the compliance officer. Fully remote onboarding is not permitted for ISIC 6430 high-risk license activities. For non-resident directors, a combination of (i) physical appearance of at least one director and (ii) videoconferenced appearance of remaining directors is acceptable only at banks' internal compliance discretion, and only after enhanced due diligence (EDD).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentified or opaque Ultimate Beneficial Owner structure in the family office trust or foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed/foundation charter; UBO declaration under CBO EDD form; passport copies of all beneficiaries; tax-residency certificates; a written explanation of the ownership waterfall; independent legal opinion confirming control and economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth for initial capital injection from overseas family members
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-24 months audited bank statements; sale-and-purchase agreements; inheritance documents; audited financial statements of source companies; notarized source-of-wealth report prepared by an external auditor; evidence of tax clearance or settlement in the source jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hit on a family member or indirect shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced screening output from Dow Jones / World-Check; explanatory narrative from the compliance institution; official police/court clearance; risk-mitigation plan; no-facilitation letter from the concerned family head; independent risk counsel advisory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: MFO authorization/license under suspicion (CA or CMA activity beyond registered scope)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official license (e.g., FSA/CMA registration or exemption letter); CBO no-objection correspondence; board resolution confirming business scope; AML/CFT policy manual; designation of a compliance officer and MLRO with CBO-approved qualifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction clients embedded in the discretionary portfolio
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client-specific risk assessment; transactional source-of-funds documentation; sanctions screening of all secondary beneficiaries; residence/visa proof; escalated approval from bank's head-office compliance; retention of a third-party due diligence report (e.g., KYC360 or Refinitiv).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 with a purpose code indicating 'Capital Injection for SPC Equity' (e.g., C1 or S100 equivalent). The beneficiary must be the Omani SPC's CBO-licensed bank account, and the remittance must include the beneficiary's IBAN, Bank Muscat/NBO, and a valid tax identification number. The receiving bank will verify the source of funds against the EDD file; post-receipt, the funds are settled through Oman's RTGS (Central Bank of Oman's Electronic Clearing System) and can be transferred to an operational account after fulfilling capital escrow release conditions. No CBO prior authorization is required for non-resident equity injection, but banks must submit a domestic money-laundering report if the amount exceeds OMR 20,000 (or USD equivalent) until the source is established.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for non-documentary transfers (e.g., investment management fees, profit distributions). Documentary trade settlements are structured as commercial letters of credit under UCP600 (sight or term) with the Omani issuing bank routing through CBO's trade finance lane. For cross-currency settlement, the transaction chain is an OMR/USD FX conversion followed by a USD correspondent transfer via CHIPS or Fedwire. Local OMR-based payments within Oman are cleared via the Oman Electronic Clearing System (OECS); cross-GCC payments can be routed using the GCC-RTGS interoperability, but SWIFT remains the primary rail. Banks require a valid export/import invoice, bill of lading, and the corresponding CBO declaration for any trade disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OMR/USD outright forward (on-premised deliverable, tenor up to 24 months)
Cross-currency ISDA-compliant swap between OMR and USD (interest rate + principal, permitted for notional hedging)
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on EUR/GBP/JPY when paired with USD as the underlying external exposure of the family office
Forwards on Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) currencies (SAR, AED, KWD) via established correspondent bank lines
Structured Shari'ah-compliant hedging forwards (Wa'ad / Murabaha) for Islamic finance booking and jumbo asset protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Annual Renewal (Renewal of Registration Certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) – Directorate General of Commercial Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of certificate issuance; renewal must be completed on or before expiry date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of 50% of the registration fee; non-renewal beyond 3 months of expiry triggers administrative strike-off and cessation of legal capacity until reinstated

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements Filing (Article 78, Commercial Companies Law RD 18/2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MoCIIP – Companies Affairs Directorate (via Invest Oman one-stop-shop)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing attracts court-imposed fine of OMR 500 to OMR 5,000 (USD 1,300 to USD 13,000); directors remain personally liable; registration renewals may be blocked

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Tax Declaration and Audited Accounts Attachment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA) – General Secretariat of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 April for 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of OMR 1,000 (USD 2,600) plus OMR 100 (USD 260) for each additional 30 days of delay; late-payment monthly interest of 1% on assessed tax; strike-off referral for chronic default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation (Ministerial Decision No. 168/2020)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MoCIIP – Companies Registry (compliance module within Commercial Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed together with Commercial Register renewal; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to OMR 5,000 (USD 13,000) for false, incomplete or overdue UBO disclosure; repeated breach leads to register suspension and strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CMA Investment Business Annual Regulatory Return (for licensed Multi-Family Office / Fund Manager)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Capital Market Authority of Oman (CMA) – Supervision and Inspections Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of fiscal year-end; professional license renewal in the month preceding annual expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission exposes the license to suspension; CMA may impose administrative fines up to OMR 10,000 (USD 26,000) and revoke the investment business license for aggravated default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Report (High-Risk Designated Non-Financial Business)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) – Central Bank of Oman
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the reporting calendar year, or as specified in the license conditions under Royal Decree 30/2016
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to OMR 50,000 (USD 130,000), license revocation and/or criminal liability for compliance officers under the AML Law; individual directors may face imprisonment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Zakat Annual Declaration (only where any Omani or GCC natural-person shareholding exists)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Secretariat General for Zakat – Diwan of Royal Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; N/A for a 100% foreign-owned SPC with no Omani/GCC capital component
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not applicable to the present foreign-owned SPC; if Omani/GCC shareholders are introduced, failure to file attracts 1% annual tithe assessment plus statutory late penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size exemption applies to SPC/LLC under Omani law: every commercial company must appoint a licensed auditor and file audited financial statements with MoCIIP under Article 78 CCL; CMA-licensed fund managers must additionally have the annual return audited by a CMA-approved auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Oman (mandatory for all entities under the Commercial Companies Law); CMA investment funds and fund managers apply IFRS plus additional CMA prudential and valuation guidance

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SPC must hold a complete and current UBO register from incorporation; annual confirmation accompanies the Commercial Register renewal and any change in control or beneficial ownership is disclosed to the Companies Registry within 15 days; the UBO register is open to inspection by MoCIIP, OTA and FIU on request
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (single-member ledger with share transfers)
Register of Share Transfer Preferences / Encumbrances
Minute Book (shareholder resolutions and manager decisions)
Register of Contracts with Interested Parties

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,300 to USD 2,600 per annum (full-service registered agent including CR renewal, PRO services and corporate secretarial support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 9,000 per annum for a licensed audit of a holding/portfolio advisory SPC with multi-family office activity and CMA reporting obligations
